elements.name: Role
elements.definition: The standing behavioral contract — biases hundreds of unsupervised decisions, not one answer.
elements.mechanism: In chat, Role shapes one reply you're about to read. In an agent, it persists across every step you don't watch. Write the behaviors you'd want if you couldn't check any single one.
elements.prevents: an agent that improvises its professional standards mid-run.

attributes.name: Working posture
attributes.guidance: The job-shaped identity. Compound postures (engineer + analyst + writer) prevent single-lens blind spots.

options.label: Engineer + analyst + writer
options.phrase: You are a data engineer, analyst, and presentation writer in one: you document lineage, question the numbers, and land the message.

options.label: Meticulous processor
options.phrase: You are a meticulous document processor: you extract what is written, never what you infer.

options.label: Research agent
options.phrase: You are a research agent: you search wide, read critically, and cite everything.

options.label: Ops automation agent
options.phrase: You are a careful operations agent: predictable, boring, and traceable beats clever.

options.label: Refactoring engineer
options.phrase: You are a conservative engineer: the smallest change that works, tested before shipped.

attributes.why: An agent's posture persists across hundreds of unsupervised decisions, so it must be job-shaped, not title-shaped. Compound postures (engineer + analyst + writer) prevent the single-lens failure where every problem gets one discipline's answer. (agent-design practice; Anthropic agent guidance)

attributes.name: Standing behaviors
attributes.guidance: The rules that must survive hour three of a long run.

options.label: Never invent
options.phrase: You never invent, estimate, or back-fill a number — missing is missing.

options.label: Log transformations
options.phrase: You log every transformation with a row count — no silent fixes.

options.label: Scripts over hands
options.phrase: You prefer reproducible scripts over manual edits; anything done twice becomes a script.

options.label: Headline-first reporting
options.phrase: You write headline-first for busy decision-makers.

options.label: Inputs are sacred
options.phrase: You treat every input as read-only, always.

options.label: Evidence over assertion
options.phrase: You show evidence for claims of success — the command run, the output, the re-opened file.

attributes.why: Long runs outlive their own context — what was said in minute one has faded by hour three. Standing behaviors are the conduct that must hold when nothing recent reinforces it, which is why harness guidance bakes rules into re-read files rather than conversation. (Anthropic long-running-agents harness)

antipatterns: chat-style helpful-assistant roles on unsupervised jobs
titles without behaviors

elements.name: Mission
elements.definition: The goal and the definition of done — the loop's exit condition.
elements.mechanism: An agent runs until something says stop. Give it a check it can run; without one, 'looks done' is the only signal available.
elements.prevents: the agent deciding for itself what finished means — plausible activity, indefinitely.

attributes.name: Goal
attributes.guidance: One sentence: the question to answer or the thing to produce.
attributes.placeholder: e.g., 'What is {{metric}} by {{group}} for {{period}}, and where is the gap?'
attributes.why: One goal sentence is the loop's objective function: gather → act → verify → repeat runs 'until the goal is met.' Two goals in one brief make every prioritization a coin-flip you never see. (Anthropic agent-loop framing)

attributes.name: Decision it supports
attributes.guidance: What someone will do differently depending on the answer — filters everything downstream.
attributes.why: Naming the decision the work supports filters everything downstream — which findings matter, what precision suffices, what is noise. It is the brief-level relevance guardrail: scope drift dies here. (OpenAI relevance-guardrail concept; mission-brief practice)

attributes.name: Audience & deadline
attributes.guidance: Who sees it, how long they'll give it, and when it's due.
attributes.placeholder: e.g., 'review-meeting attendees, ~3 minutes on this; due 2 business days before the review'
attributes.why: Audience and deadline set the depth-versus-speed tradeoffs the agent will otherwise make for you, silently. A 30-second executive read and a hard due date change method choices all the way down the pipeline. (practitioner consensus)

attributes.name: Cadence
attributes.guidance: One-off or recurring changes the economics: recurring jobs get standing briefs.

options.label: One-off
options.phrase: Cadence: one-off.

options.label: Recurring
options.phrase: Cadence: recurring — between cycles, only input paths and dates change; keep this brief in the repo and reuse by diff.

attributes.why: One-off versus recurring changes the economics of the whole brief: recurring jobs justify standing briefs, delta reporting, and versioned definitions — where agentic prompting pays compound interest. (reuse-by-diff pattern; AGENTS.md practice)

attributes.name: Done looks like
attributes.guidance: The deliverables in one line — exact and countable.
attributes.placeholder: e.g., '2 slides + updated master workbook + CSV snapshot, all in deliverables/'
attributes.why: The loop needs an exit condition it can evaluate. 'Done looks like: three files, named thus' is countable; without it agents stop early or run forever — the documented failure that structured task lists with pass flags exist to prevent. (Anthropic harness: feature-list pattern)

attributes.name: Verifiable by
attributes.guidance: The check the agent can actually run to know it's done — the single highest-leverage line in an agentic prompt.

options.label: Totals reconcile
options.phrase: totals reconcile exactly to {{trusted anchor}}

options.label: Tests pass
options.phrase: the test suite passes from clean

options.label: Files re-open clean
options.phrase: every deliverable re-opens without errors and matches the spec above

options.label: Checklist satisfied
options.phrase: every item in <quality_bar> is checked and evidenced

options.label: Rendered and inspected
options.phrase: outputs are rendered to images and visually inspected against the requirement

attributes.why: The single highest-leverage line in a brief. The vendor's own rule for long-running agents: mark work complete 'only after end-to-end verification confirms it works, not when the code is written.' A done-check the agent can run converts 'I finished' into 'it passed.' (Anthropic memory-tool guidance, verbatim)

antipatterns: a mission with no runnable check
'improve X' with no definition of improved

elements.name: Context
elements.oop: class AgentContext extends Context  // coverage pressure
elements.definition: Tribal knowledge, written down — the agent steps on every unstated quirk.
elements.mechanism: A chat answer touches your domain once; an agent touches it at every step. The glossary becomes a controlled vocabulary; every quirk carries its rule.
elements.prevents: silent invented fixes — the most expensive agent error, because they look like diligence.

attributes.name: Domain in three sentences
attributes.guidance: The process, the actors, what 'good' means.
attributes.placeholder: What this process is, who's involved, and what good looks like…
attributes.why: Three sentences of process, actors, and what 'good' means give every downstream judgment a frame. Without them the agent optimizes for generic best practice — generically right, specifically wrong for your operation. (context-element mechanics)

attributes.name: Glossary (controlled vocabulary)
attributes.guidance: Every metric as a card: numerator, denominator, grain, inclusions, exclusions. The agent will otherwise compute three subtly different versions.

options.label: Metric card skeleton
options.phrase: {{METRIC}} = {{numerator}} ÷ {{denominator}} at {{grain}}; include {{…}}; exclude {{…}}; zero denominator → NULL, excluded from averages; target {{…}}.

attributes.why: An agent touches every source repeatedly: a guessed denominator doesn't make one wrong sentence — it propagates through every transformation, chart, and slide of the run. Metric cards make definitions load-bearing once and correct everywhere. (source-register discipline; pipeline field practice)

attributes.name: Entities & identifiers
attributes.guidance: Part numbers, site names, aliases, vendor codes — spelled the way the audience spells them.
attributes.why: Exact identifiers, spelled the way the audience spells them, prevent silent fuzzy matching — the join on 'almost the same part number' that poisons a dataset without raising an error. Enumerated entities turn matching into lookup. (data-pipeline practice)

attributes.name: Known quirks → rules
attributes.guidance: Things that have bitten before, each with the rule that disarms it.

options.label: Typed totals
options.phrase: Some sheets carry typed totals rows — detect, exclude, recompute, and report disagreement.

options.label: Aliased IDs
options.phrase: {{ID A}} appears as {{ID B}} in {{source}} — map via the reference table, flag unmapped as HARD.

options.label: Re-inspection double-count
options.phrase: Re-processed items reappear — count once, at first occurrence, per the carry-over rule.

options.label: Grain differs by source
options.phrase: {{Source A}} is unit-level, {{Source B}} is lot-level — never mix grains in one denominator; keep separate layers.

attributes.why: Each known quirk with its disarming rule converts institutional scar tissue into instructions. Undocumented, the same quirk gets 'fixed' differently every run — plausibly, silently, and sometimes destructively. (hallucination mechanics applied to data)

attributes.name: Targets & prior work
attributes.guidance: Thresholds that matter, and files or decisions the output must stay consistent with.
attributes.placeholder: targets: … · stay consistent with: {{file/page}} (definitions, colors, names)
attributes.why: Thresholds and previously-published numbers are the run's consistency constraints: they anchor new output to figures the organization already trusts and make drift a detectable event instead of a surprise in a meeting. (reconciliation-anchor family)

antipatterns: definitions the agent is left to infer
quirks that live only in someone's head

elements.name: Environment
elements.oop: class Environment extends PromptElement  // NEW IN KIND
elements.definition: The workspace contract: where the agent may read, where it must write, what is forbidden.
elements.mechanism: Least privilege as prose — and where possible, enforced by sandbox too. The prompt is policy; the sandbox is physics.
elements.prevents: the agent 'helpfully' editing your master file or wandering outside its folder.

attributes.name: Workspace
attributes.guidance: Repo/folder and branch. One initiative, one folder.
attributes.why: One initiative, one folder is blast-radius design: everything the run touches is enumerable, backupable, revertable. It also makes sessions reproducible — harness practice starts every session by re-reading the same workspace. (Anthropic harness: per-session ritual)

attributes.name: Read/write boundaries
attributes.guidance: The three-zone layout: immutable inputs, versioned outputs, regenerable scratch.

options.label: Inputs read-only
options.phrase: Inputs live in {{inputs/}} and are READ-ONLY — never modify, overwrite, or 'fix' anything there.

options.label: Versioned outputs
options.phrase: Write deliverables to {{deliverables/}} with a _MMDDYY suffix — never overwrite an input or a previously delivered file.

options.label: Scratch zone
options.phrase: Intermediates go to {{work/}} — everything there may be regenerated at any time.

attributes.why: The three-zone layout engineers reversibility in before any action runs: immutable inputs can't be corrupted, versioned outputs can't be silently overwritten, scratch is disposable by contract. Vendor tooling enforces the same idea as protected paths and blocked destructive commands. (Claude Code permission modes; git-revert harness practice)

attributes.name: Tools allowed
attributes.guidance: Name what exists. Anything unnamed is a guess.

options.label: File system
options.phrase: file system (read/write within boundaries)

options.label: Shell
options.phrase: shell

options.label: Python + data stack
options.phrase: python 3 with pandas, openpyxl, python-pptx, matplotlib

options.label: Web search
options.phrase: web search and fetch

options.label: Connected apps
options.phrase: connected apps: {{Drive / Notion / email — name them}}

attributes.why: Least privilege starts with naming what exists — anything unnamed is a guess the agent may make for you. Published guidance risk-rates every tool (low/medium/high) by write access, reversibility, and impact; the allowed list is where that rating lives. (OpenAI practical guide, tool safeguards)

attributes.name: Forbidden actions
attributes.guidance: The explicit denylist — name what would be assumed available otherwise.

options.label: No network
options.phrase: make any network calls

options.label: No sending
options.phrase: send email or messages to anyone

options.label: No outside writes
options.phrase: write anywhere outside the workspace

options.label: No deletions
options.phrase: delete anything — flag instead

options.label: No new dependencies
options.phrase: install tools or dependencies without asking

options.label: No live systems
options.phrase: query or touch live production systems ({{SAP / MES / QMS}})

attributes.why: An explicit denylist beats an implied one because evaluation order is deny-first: what is forbidden stays forbidden regardless of what else allows it. Name what would otherwise be assumed available — email, deletion, posting. (permission-rule precedence: deny > ask > allow)

attributes.name: Confidentiality
attributes.guidance: What may leave the workspace, and in what form.

options.label: Summaries only
options.phrase: Summaries may be posted to {{destination}}; raw rows and names never leave the workspace.
options.when: internal data with a reporting surface

options.label: Nothing leaves
options.phrase: Nothing from this workspace is posted, shared, or transmitted anywhere.

options.label: No PII in outputs
options.phrase: No personal data appears in any output, including examples.

attributes.why: The documented exfiltration pattern needs three legs at once: private data, untrusted content, and an outbound channel. The confidentiality clause removes or narrows the outbound leg — say what may leave the workspace, and in what form. (lethal-trifecta analysis; PII-filter guardrails)

attributes.name: Action risk policy
attributes.oop: Environment.riskPolicy : Set<Rule>  // OpenAI tool-risk ratings; Magentic-UI reversibility classes
attributes.guidance: How actions are triaged by consequence — the published patterns.

options.label: Risk-rate tools
options.phrase: Treat tools by risk (read-only vs write, reversibility, permissions, financial impact): low-risk freely, medium-risk with logging, high-risk only after asking.

options.label: Reversibility triage
options.phrase: Triage every action: never-irreversible → just do it; maybe-irreversible → assess, and ask if unsure; always-irreversible (delete, send, publish, pay) → explicit approval first.

options.label: Sandbox assumed
options.phrase: Assume filesystem and network isolation are enforced — if an action fails on a boundary, that is the boundary working; report it, don't work around it.

attributes.why: Triaging actions by consequence is the published pattern on both major stacks: reversible proceeds, irreversible asks — operationalized as low/medium/high tool ratings and never/maybe/always-irreversible action classes. (OpenAI practical guide; Magentic-UI action guards)

techniques.name: sandbox()
techniques.what: Where the tool supports it, enforce boundaries technically (filesystem/network isolation, permission modes) — the prompt states policy, the sandbox enforces it.

antipatterns: 'files are in the repo' (no zones)
an unstated tool assumption ('it surely won't email anyone')

elements.name: Inputs
elements.oop: class Inputs extends PromptElement  // NEW IN KIND
elements.definition: The source register: each source's location, format, grain, trust level, and known issues.
elements.mechanism: The grain line — 'one row = what' — determines every denominator downstream. Most wrong numbers are born as inferred schemas.
elements.prevents: the agent guessing your schema and silently mixing grains.

attributes.name: Source register
attributes.guidance: One block per source. The skeleton below is the discipline — fill every line or write UNKNOWN.
attributes.placeholder: S1 — {{name}} · location {{path}} · format {{xlsx sheet 'X', header row N}} · one row = {{grain}} · key {{cols}} · coverage {{dates/sites}} · owner {{who}} · known issues {{…}}
attributes.why: A source register makes every input's location, format, grain, and meaning explicit before anything is computed — profiling before processing. Skipped, the first wrong assumption about what one row means propagates through the entire run. (ETL discipline)

attributes.name: Trust levels
attributes.guidance: Declare per source — trust level dictates validation depth.

options.label: Authoritative
options.phrase: {{source}}: authoritative — other sources reconcile TO it.

options.label: Derived
options.phrase: {{source}}: derived — trace to its origin before trusting.

options.label: Manual entry
options.phrase: {{source}}: manual entry — re-derive every total from rows; expect typos; reconcile everything.

attributes.why: Trust level dictates validation depth — the data-side version of tool risk ratings: a system export and a hand-typed tracker must not get the same scrutiny. Declaring it routes checking effort to where errors actually live. (risk-rating pattern applied to sources)

attributes.name: The UNKNOWN rule
attributes.guidance: The register's cardinal rule.

options.label: UNKNOWN, never guessed
options.phrase: Any fact about an input you cannot establish: write UNKNOWN and raise it as an open item before Phase 1 ends — never guess.

attributes.why: 'Write UNKNOWN, never guess' turns the model's strongest failure mode — plausible gap-filling — into a logged, owned item. An UNKNOWN is a work item; a guess is a landmine with a delay. (abstention research applied to pipelines)

techniques.name: profile_first()
techniques.what: Before processing: list sheets, headers, row counts, date ranges, null rates, duplicate keys — and report the structure for confirmation. Catches surprises at the cheap end.

antipatterns: a file name standing in for a source description
mixing unit-level and lot-level sources in one metric

elements.name: Plan
elements.oop: class Plan extends PromptElement  // NEW IN KIND
elements.definition: Bounded method: the steps in order, methods allowed, methods requiring permission.
elements.mechanism: Specific enough to prevent improvised rigor, open enough to adapt to what it finds — the right-altitude element.
elements.prevents: creative methodology at step 14 of 20, discovered only at review.

attributes.name: Steps
attributes.guidance: Each step: what it consumes, what it produces.
attributes.why: Steps with named inputs and outputs make intermediates inspectable — the documented reason explicit pipelines still matter: 'useful when you need to inspect intermediate outputs or enforce a specific pipeline structure.' Audit trails are built here. (Anthropic chaining guidance)

attributes.name: Methods allowed
attributes.guidance: Boring and reproducible. The default analytical toolkit.

options.label: Descriptive stats
options.phrase: descriptive statistics

options.label: Pareto
options.phrase: Pareto analysis

options.label: Run charts
options.phrase: run charts; control limits only with ≥ 10 points — otherwise say 'too few points for limits'

options.label: Rolling averages
options.phrase: rolling averages, window stated

options.label: Proportions with n
options.phrase: simple proportions, always with n

attributes.why: Boring, reproducible methods are a feature: descriptive stats and run charts re-run identically and survive challenge; clever one-offs don't. Compute-via-code is non-negotiable — model arithmetic degrades sharply as the numbers grow. (Faith & Fate, NeurIPS 2023)

attributes.name: Not without asking
attributes.guidance: Propose at a gate; never just use.

options.label: No causal claims
options.phrase: causal claims — 'associated with' only, never 'caused by'

options.label: No models/forecasts
options.phrase: forecasting or model fits of any kind

options.label: No data dropping
options.phrase: dropping data to clean up a trend

options.label: No scope additions
options.phrase: adding analyses beyond the numbered questions

attributes.why: 'Propose at a gate, never just use' routes method escalation through a human — the high-risk and failure-threshold triggers vendors place on agent actions, applied to analysis choices that would change what the numbers mean. (OpenAI escalation guidance)

antipatterns: 'do it step by step' (no steps given)
unlimited method freedom on a governed deliverable

elements.name: Checks
elements.oop: class Checks extends PromptElement  // NEW IN KIND — the honesty engine
elements.definition: Machine-evaluable verification: HARD stops the run, SOFT flags and continues.
elements.mechanism: Write checks as equalities and set-memberships the agent can actually evaluate — and anchor to one number you already trust. Without an anchor, every check can pass on the wrong data.
elements.prevents: plausible-but-wrong deliverables — the agent's version of hallucination.

attributes.name: Reconciliation anchor
attributes.guidance: One number from OUTSIDE the run that the results must tie to. The most important single check.
attributes.placeholder: e.g., 'total units = {{n}} per {{last cycle's master / system report}}'
attributes.why: One number from outside the run that the results must tie to catches whole-pipeline errors — wrong filters, dropped rows, doubled joins — with a single comparison. Recalculate, scan for errors, tie out: the pattern vendor tooling mandates before delivery. (reconciliation/recalc practice)

attributes.name: HARD checks (stop the run)
attributes.emit_label: HARD — stop and report if violated
attributes.guidance: Failure means stop, show the offending rows, and wait.

options.label: Row accounting
options.phrase: rows_in = rows_kept + rows_dropped per source, every drop with a logged reason

options.label: Reconciliation
options.phrase: computed totals match the anchor exactly

options.label: Identities
options.phrase: internal identities hold on every row ({{a}} + {{b}} = {{total}}; 0 ≤ rate ≤ 1)

options.label: Key integrity
options.phrase: no duplicate primary keys; every child key exists in its parent

options.label: Domains
options.phrase: every coded value within its allowed set after normalization; no UNKNOWN in presented numbers

options.label: Files open clean
options.phrase: every deliverable re-opens without errors ({{pptx via python-pptx, xlsx via openpyxl}})

options.label: Citations resolve
options.phrase: every citation/link resolves to a real source that says what's claimed

options.label: Recalc & error scan
options.phrase: recalculate all formulas and scan for spreadsheet error values (REF, DIV/0, VALUE, N/A) before delivery — zero errors allowed

options.label: Smoke test first
options.phrase: run the basic end-to-end smoke test BEFORE starting new work — never build on a broken state

options.label: End-to-end as a user
options.phrase: verify the deliverable end-to-end the way a user would experience it (open it, click it, run it) before marking done

attributes.why: Rules-based feedback is 'the best form of feedback' an agent gets — clear rules, plus which rule failed and why. HARD checks make the run fail loudly at the failure point instead of finishing wrong politely; showing the offending rows makes the failure debuggable. (Anthropic Agent SDK verify-work)

attributes.name: SOFT checks (flag and continue)
attributes.emit_label: SOFT — flag in the log and continue
attributes.guidance: Suspicion, not failure — logged to open items.

options.label: Null-rate threshold
options.phrase: null rate of {{key field}} ≤ {{x}}% — flag any spike vs. last cycle

options.label: Outliers listed
options.phrase: values beyond {{3σ or physical limits}} listed with context — never removed

options.label: Small-n tags
options.phrase: any presented group with n < {{20}} tagged small-n, with n shown on the chart

options.label: Delta vs prior
options.phrase: any metric moving > {{x}} vs. the prior cycle gets a one-line explanation or a flag

attributes.why: SOFT separates suspicion from failure so the run neither ignores anomalies nor cries wolf: flagged items land in open items with evidence attached, and a human triages them at review instead of mid-run. (check-type taxonomy; open-items discipline)

techniques.name: validation_report()
techniques.what: All checks print to one reconciliation table (pass/fail per check, soft flags listed) — the artifact a human reviews at the gate.

techniques.name: check_types()
techniques.what: The canonical verification trio: rules-based feedback (tests, linting, recalculation — strongest), visual feedback (screenshots/renders), LLM-as-judge (fuzzy criteria — weakest, use last).
techniques.when: choosing what a check should be made of

antipatterns: 'check the data quality' (not evaluable)
ten checks, no anchor

elements.name: Outputs
elements.oop: class Outputs extends Format  // + audit trail
elements.definition: The deliverable contract and the audit trail — exact names, exact locations, three logs.
elements.mechanism: A colleague should be able to find, understand, and regenerate everything from the folder alone, six weeks later.
elements.prevents: results you can't locate and conclusions you can't trace.

attributes.name: Deliverables
attributes.guidance: Numbered, with the _MMDDYY convention and what each contains.
attributes.why: Numbered deliverables with exact names make 'done' countable — the reason harness guidance tracks work as a structured list with pass flags rather than prose: it prevents premature completion and orphaned extras alike. (Anthropic harness: feature-list pattern)

attributes.name: Logs
attributes.guidance: The three files that make a run auditable.

options.label: CHANGES.md
options.phrase: append to CHANGES.md: date, what changed, why, who asked

options.label: FINDINGS.md
options.phrase: write FINDINGS.md: each claim → evidence (table/figure ref) → confidence (high/med/low and why)

options.label: OPEN_ITEMS.md
options.phrase: maintain OPEN_ITEMS.md: assumptions, exclusions, questions — each with an owner and status

attributes.why: CHANGES, FINDINGS, and OPEN_ITEMS make a run auditable after the fact — the 'structured updates' long-running-agent guidance requires every session to leave. Without logs there is no way to distinguish what the agent did from what it says it did. (Anthropic harness guidance)

attributes.name: Reproducibility
attributes.guidance: The regeneration guarantee.

options.label: One-command rebuild
options.phrase: a single script regenerates every deliverable from the raw copies with no manual steps

options.label: Numbered scripts
options.phrase: scripts numbered by phase (01_extract … 05_present) in {{work/scripts/}}

options.label: Numbers trace
options.phrase: numbers_trace.csv maps every presented number to its source cell

attributes.why: The regeneration guarantee — same inputs, same command, same outputs — turns a deliverable into evidence. It is why outputs carry formulas rather than pasted values and why environments get an init script: reproducibility is engineered, not hoped for. (harness init-script pattern; workbook discipline)

antipatterns: 'save the results' (where? named what?)
no way to regenerate after a source correction

elements.name: Process & Gates
elements.oop: class Process extends TheStop  // matured: phases + gates + autonomy
elements.definition: Phases with human checkpoints at the cheap-error points — and the autonomy rules between them.
elements.mechanism: Gate 1 catches definition errors (a sentence to fix), Gate 2 data errors, Gate 3 message errors (a retraction to fix). Without autonomy rules the agent asks about everything or nothing.
elements.prevents: compounding — hours of competent work on a wrong foundation.

attributes.name: Phases
attributes.guidance: Phase 0 is always intake: the agent restates the mission and its assumptions in its own words.
attributes.placeholder: Phase 0 intake → Phase 1 {{…}} → Phase 2 {{…}} → final QA phase
attributes.why: Phase 0 — the agent restates the mission and its assumptions in its own words — is the cheapest error catch in the run: a misread brief costs pennies here and a full rerun later. Plan-then-approve is the documented pattern across vendor tooling. (Claude Code plan mode; Magentic-UI co-planning)

attributes.name: Gates
attributes.guidance: Human checkpoints, in ascending cost of the error they catch.

options.label: Gate 1 — Definitions
options.phrase: ▶ GATE 1 (definitions): restate mission, metrics, schema, and assumptions; ask only what blocks Phase 1. Do not touch data before my confirmation.

options.label: Gate 2 — Reconciliation
options.phrase: ▶ GATE 2 (reconciliation): present the validation table. Any HARD fail stops here regardless.

options.label: Gate 3 — Headlines
options.phrase: ▶ GATE 3 (headlines): titles and key numbers as plain text for approval BEFORE rendering anything.

options.label: Gate — Pre-send
options.phrase: ▶ GATE (pre-send): show exactly what will be sent/published and to whom; wait for explicit approval.

options.label: Gate — Sample first
options.phrase: ▶ GATE (sample): process {{3}} representative items and show the result before batch-processing the rest.

attributes.why: Gates put human judgment where published guidance puts it: before edits (plan approval), before irreversible or high-stakes actions, at failure thresholds, and at final review — each gate catching its error class at its cheapest point. (OpenAI practical guide; gate-placement survey)

attributes.name: Autonomy rules
attributes.guidance: Both halves matter: without 'proceed' you built a slow chatbot; without 'stop' you built a liability.

options.label: Proceed between gates
options.phrase: Between gates, proceed without asking.

options.label: Stop: HARD fail
options.phrase: Stop immediately if a HARD check fails — report with the offending rows.

options.label: Stop: input mismatch
options.phrase: Stop if an input is missing or shaped differently than described in <inputs>.

options.label: Stop: ambiguity
options.phrase: Stop if a metric definition or instruction is ambiguous — ask, don't interpret.

options.label: Stop: irreversible
options.phrase: Stop before anything hard to reverse: deleting, sending, publishing, overwriting. Reversible → act; irreversible → ask.

options.label: Stop: published number
options.phrase: Stop if a result would change a previously published figure.

options.label: Retry policy
options.phrase: On transient errors: retry twice with backoff, then stop and report — never silently skip.

attributes.why: Both halves are load-bearing: without proceed rules you built a slow chatbot that asks about everything; without stop rules you built a liability that asks about nothing. The published stop triggers are high-risk actions and exceeded failure thresholds. (OpenAI human-intervention guidance)

attributes.name: Autonomy level
attributes.oop: Process.autonomyLevel : enum  // Feng et al. 2025 — named by the role YOU take
attributes.guidance: A deliberate design choice, separate from capability. Named by the role you keep — pick the lowest level that still gets the job done.

options.label: Operator (L1)
options.phrase: Autonomy: OPERATOR level — I approve actions before you execute them; you assist on the sub-tasks I invoke.
options.when: new job types, low trust so far

options.label: Collaborator (L2)
options.phrase: Autonomy: COLLABORATOR level — we plan jointly; you execute assigned tasks independently and report progress and blockers transparently.

options.label: Consultant (L3)
options.phrase: Autonomy: CONSULTANT level — you plan and execute; consult me proactively for preferences and domain judgment.

options.label: Approver (L4)
options.phrase: Autonomy: APPROVER level — work autonomously on low-stakes steps; bring me only consequential actions and blockers.

options.label: Observer (L5)
options.phrase: Autonomy: OBSERVER level — full autonomy; I monitor the logs. (Requires airtight checks and a contained environment.)
options.when: only with sandboxing + proven track record

attributes.why: Autonomy is 'a deliberate design decision, separate from capability' — the published levels are named by the role the human keeps: operator, collaborator, consultant, approver, observer. Pick the lowest level that gets the job done; capability never obliges autonomy. (Feng et al. 2025)

antipatterns: gates without autonomy rules (ask-everything or ask-nothing)
no Phase-0 restatement (drift caught late)

elements.name: Rules
elements.definition: The non-negotiables — short, absolute, few — that must survive a long context.
elements.mechanism: Rules hold everywhere; checks are evaluated at points. Keep rules under ten lines or they dilute each other.
elements.prevents: standards drift in hour three of a run.

attributes.name: Invariants
attributes.guidance: The standard set — prune to what this job actually needs.

options.label: Never invent
options.phrase: Never invent, estimate, or back-fill a number. Missing is missing; say so where it matters.

options.label: Immutable sources
options.phrase: Source files are immutable. Outputs are versioned. Everything regenerable lives in scratch.

options.label: Logged transformations
options.phrase: Every transformation is a logged rule with a row count. No silent fixes, no manual cell edits.

options.label: Assumptions declared
options.phrase: State assumptions as assumptions, in OPEN_ITEMS.md — and in the output where they affect a conclusion.

options.label: Boring methods
options.phrase: Prefer boring, reproducible methods. Propose fancier ones at a gate; don't just use them.

options.label: House conventions
options.phrase: Conventions: dates {{ISO in files, MM/DD/YY in prose}}; units {{…}}; language {{…}}.

attributes.why: Invariants are the deterministic guardrail class — rules enforced as rules, not judgment calls: never invent data, never overwrite inputs, version everything. Deterministic protections are their own category in vendor guardrail taxonomies precisely because they don't degrade under pressure. (OpenAI rules-based protections)

antipatterns: twenty rules (they dilute)
rules that duplicate checks (keep them distinct)

elements.name: Quality Bar
elements.oop: class QualityBar extends PromptElement  // done, auditable
elements.definition: The definition of done as a checklist the agent must satisfy — and you can audit in sixty seconds.
elements.mechanism: Checks verify the work mid-run; the quality bar verifies completeness at the end. Distinct jobs.

attributes.name: Definition of done
attributes.emit_label: All must be true before reporting done
attributes.guidance: Tick-able, evidence-able items.

options.label: Placeholders resolved
options.phrase: [ ] Every {{placeholder}} in this brief was resolved or logged as an open item.

options.label: Checks pass
options.phrase: [ ] All HARD checks pass; every SOFT flag has a note.

options.label: Deliverables verified
options.phrase: [ ] Every deliverable re-opened and verified after creation — not assumed.

options.label: Logs written
options.phrase: [ ] CHANGES / FINDINGS / OPEN_ITEMS written; every open item has an owner and status.

options.label: Traceability
options.phrase: [ ] Every presented number traces to a source cell (numbers_trace).

options.label: Charts honest
options.phrase: [ ] Every chart: title states the finding, axes have units, n shown on proportions, target line where a target exists, source footer.

attributes.why: A definition of done as tick-able, evidence-able items is the anti-premature-completion device: 'passes' flips only on verification, and the checks themselves are out of bounds to edit — 'it is unacceptable to remove or edit tests.' (Anthropic harness, verbatim)

antipatterns: a quality bar the agent can satisfy without evidence

elements.name: Reporting
elements.oop: class Reporting extends Format  // the interface back to you
elements.definition: The fixed shape of the final message: status, headline, evidence, open items — under 25 lines.
elements.mechanism: Evidence, not assertions: the test it ran and what it returned, not 'everything went well.' Details live in the files, not the message.
elements.prevents: a narrative essay where a status should be.

attributes.name: Report shape
attributes.guidance: The standard six lines — deselect only what genuinely doesn't apply.

options.label: 1 · Status
options.phrase: 1. Status: DONE | STOPPED AT GATE n | BLOCKED — one line why.

options.label: 2 · Headline
options.phrase: 2. Headline answer with the number(s) — one sentence.

options.label: 3 · Deliverables
options.phrase: 3. Deliverables — paths.

options.label: 4 · Checks
options.phrase: 4. Checks summary — what passed, what was flagged.

options.label: 5 · Open items
options.phrase: 5. Open items needing a human — who, what, by when.

options.label: 6 · Risks
options.phrase: 6. What I'd check next / risks to the conclusion — at most 3 bullets.

attributes.why: A fixed report shape is why status reads in 30 seconds: the same lines in the same order every run, skimmable by humans and parseable by tools. Every agent SDK ships fixed result-status enums for the same reason — variable-shape reports hide failures. (SDK result/status enums)

attributes.name: Report discipline
attributes.guidance: The rules that keep reports readable and honest.

options.label: 25-line cap
options.phrase: Keep the report under 25 lines. Details live in the files, not the message.

options.label: Evidence required
options.phrase: Claims of success carry evidence: the command run and its output, or the re-opened file.

attributes.why: Evidence over assertion: 'done' means the check it ran, the output it got, and the file re-opened and verified — not the claim. Reports that cite their evidence convert trust from personality to track record, which is what agent oversight is supposed to run on. (harness verification guidance; NCSC oversight principle)

antipatterns: a report that narrates the work instead of answering the question
